page_title: Natural Killer Cells (NKC) – Price, Purpose and Diagnosis | Metropolis Healthcare

faqs.question: What does the Natural Killer Cells Test measure?
faqs.answer: It measures the number and percentage of NK cells (CD16/CD56) in blood to support assessment of immune function.

faqs.question: Do I need to fast before this test?
Why is this test done in fertility evaluation?
faqs.answer: In selected cases, NK cell levels/activity may be assessed as part of an immune evaluation in recurrent miscarriage or implantation failure, based on specialist advice.

faqs.question: Can stress affect NK cell results?
faqs.answer: Yes. Physical or emotional stress and intense exercise can transiently alter circulating immune cell counts and distributions.

faqs.question: What method is used for this test?
faqs.answer: Flow cytometry, which identifies NK cells using CD16 and CD56 markers and reports percentage and absolute count.

faqs.question: When are NK cells considered low?
faqs.answer: When CD(16+56) falls below 5.6% or the absolute NK cell count is below 173 cells/cu.mm (lab reference ranges may vary).

faqs.question: What diseases can be associated with abnormal NK cell counts?
faqs.answer: Abnormal results may be associated with immune deficiency, immune activation/inflammation, chronic viral infections, malignancy-related immune changes, or medication effects; interpretation requires clinical correlation.
